cf.title: Don't consider FATAL errors "abnormal server termination"

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal: four participants agreed in 2025 that the appended text misleads, and demand is shown in message #1. Two fixable points remain. standards-compat-1 asks what clients that match the appended string should use instead. replication-ondisk-1 asks which libpq callers depend on the old PQstatus() timing, since v2 had to change postgres_fdw. Both need an answer from someone who knows libpq connection state, but neither requires a different proposal.

brief.title: libpq: mark connection closed on FATAL or PANIC error
brief.problem: libpq appends "server closed the connection unexpectedly / This probably means the server terminated abnormally" even after the server sent a FATAL, such as after pg_terminate_backend(). The hint misleads users into thinking Postgres crashed. It also stops clients from using PQresultErrorField on the final PGresult.
brief.proposed_design: When libpq receives a FATAL or PANIC error, it sets the connection status to CONNECTION_BAD. libpq then treats the following socket close as expected and does not append the "unexpectedly" text. v2 also changes postgres_fdw and fixes tests, and the commit message is said to explain the postgres_fdw change.
user_visible_surface: libpq no longer appends "server closed the connection unexpectedly" and the abnormal-termination hint after a FATAL or PANIC error.
PQstatus() returns CONNECTION_BAD once a FATAL or PANIC error has arrived, possibly before the socket closes.
The last PGresult after a FATAL holds the server error fields, so PQresultErrorField can read them.
postgres_fdw behavior changes in v2, but the material does not say how.
author_claims: The fix is small: mark the connection CONNECTION_BAD when a FATAL or PANIC arrives.
The appended text is wrong, because the server told the client it was closing the connection.
The appended text makes errors harder for clients to parse.
v2 fixes the test failures that cfbot found in v1.
brief.thread_state: Andres Freund, Robert Haas, Christoph Berg and Bruce Momjian agreed in 2025 that the message misleads, and Berg warned that much software parses its first line. Freund reported v1 test failures, and nobody has replied to v2, which is in its third CommitFest.
unclear: The material does not say what the postgres_fdw change in v2 is or why it is needed.
The material does not say whether v2 passes the full test suite on all platforms, including Windows.
The material does not say how clients that match "server closed the connection unexpectedly" to detect a lost connection behave after the change.
The patch does not change the message or hint for real unexpected closes, which the 2025 discussion also raised.
The material does not say how a FATAL during connection startup or inside COPY or pipeline mode behaves.

prior_attempts.title: Revert commits 290acac92b and 8a7e9e9dad.
prior_attempts.quote: We found that on Windows, the client end of the socket is not able to read the data once we close the socket in the server which leads to loss of error message which is not what we expect.
prior_attempts.reason:
This commit revert the commits to add a test case that tests the 'force'
option when there is an active backend connected to the database being
dropped.

This feature internally sends SIGTERM to all the backends connected to the
database being dropped and then the same is reported to the client.  We
found that on Windows, the client end of the socket is not able to read
the data once we close the socket in the server which leads to loss of
error message which is not what we expect.  We also observed  similar
behavior in other cases like pg_terminate_backend(),
pg_ctl kill TERM <pid>.  There are probably a few others like that.  The
fix for this requires further study.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 removed tests that needed the client to read the FATAL after pg_terminate_backend() or a SIGTERM, because Windows can drop that message. This proposal changes libpq only when the FATAL does arrive, so where Windows drops it the old text stays.

objections.title: Clients that match the appended string lose reconnect detection
objections.failure_scenario: An application uses a framework that detects a lost connection by matching "server closed the connection unexpectedly" and then reconnects. After its libpq is upgraded, a session ended by pg_terminate_backend() or a restart returns only the FATAL text. The framework treats it as an ordinary query error and does not retry, and operators find out from failed requests after a routine failover.
objections.argument: Message #3 lists several packages that parse this exact string to detect lost connections, and warns against changing it. The patch removes the string in the FATAL case, which is the usual case after an administrator command or a shutdown. The commit message argues the text is wrong, but it does not weigh what existing parsers lose or offer them a stable replacement. A committer would likely ask for this to be called out as a compatibility change and for the replacement to be documented.
objections.author_must_show: How should applications that match this string today detect an admin-terminated connection after the change, and will the release notes and docs say so?

critic.reasoning: Message #3 lists software that matches this exact line, and the patch removes the line in the FATAL case. The thread does not answer the warning or say that these clients have another signal, such as PQstatus() or the SQLSTATE.

objections.title: Earlier CONNECTION_BAD changes libpq API behavior for existing callers
objections.failure_scenario: An extension, or libpqwalreceiver in a logical apply worker, receives a FATAL and then checks PQstatus() or keeps calling PQgetResult() as it did before. With the patch, PQstatus() reports CONNECTION_BAD before the socket closes, so the old code path changes. The extension author finds out when the extension's tests fail or its error reporting changes on PG20.
objections.argument: v2 had to change postgres_fdw (message #7), so at least one in-tree libpq consumer depended on the old ordering. The material does not say what that change is, or whether dblink, libpqwalreceiver and the logical replication workers were checked. Out-of-tree code built on libpq would need the same change, with no compile-time signal. The commit message, the only place where the postgres_fdw change is explained, is not in the material.
objections.author_must_show: Which caller pattern did postgres_fdw rely on, and have dblink, libpqwalreceiver and the logical replication workers been checked for the same pattern?

critic.reasoning: Message #7 confirms that postgres_fdw needed a change, so the new PQstatus() timing is visible to callers. The v2 commit message that explains the change is not in the material, and nobody has reviewed v2, so the question about other callers stays open.

refuted.title: PQstatus change that broke postgres_fdw will also hit other clients
refuted.failure_scenario: A driver or extension built on libpq reacts to an error by checking PQstatus(), and expects CONNECTION_OK until a read fails, for example to send a rollback or to decide on reconnecting. With the patch, PQstatus() returns CONNECTION_BAD as soon as the FATAL arrives. The cleanup path takes a different branch, and the maintainer learns of it from user bug reports after the release.
refuted.argument: Message #7 says v2 needed a change to postgres_fdw. That shows the new PQstatus timing is visible to libpq callers. Out-of-tree callers would hit the same behaviour change and get no fix from the patch. The material does not say what postgres_fdw relied on, so nobody can judge which other callers break, and nobody has reviewed v2.
refuted.author_must_show: What did postgres_fdw assume about PQstatus after a FATAL, and how should other libpq callers with the same assumption find and fix it?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which makes the same point about PQstatus() timing and also names the in-tree callers to check.

refuted.title: Unexplained postgres_fdw change suggests other libpq clients need it too
refuted.failure_scenario: A pooler or driver built on libpq keeps reading results after a FATAL and assumes PQstatus() stays CONNECTION_OK until the socket closes. After the change, PQstatus() returns CONNECTION_BAD early, and the client takes a different error or cleanup path. Its maintainers find out from user reports after a PG20 libpq upgrade.
refuted.argument: Message #7 says the fix required a small change to postgres_fdw, which is an in-tree libpq client. The thread does not say what postgres_fdw relied on. If one in-tree client depended on the old PQstatus() timing, out-of-tree clients may depend on it as well, and nothing tells them. The commit message shown covers only v1 and does not describe the contract change for PQstatus().
refuted.author_must_show: What did postgres_fdw rely on, and which documented PQstatus() behavior should out-of-tree libpq clients expect after a FATAL?

refuted.title: String-matching clients lose their lost-connection signal after FATAL
refuted.failure_scenario: An application that detects lost connections by matching "server closed the connection unexpectedly" receives only the FATAL text after pg_terminate_backend() or a server shutdown. It no longer sees the connection as lost, so it does not reconnect or retry. Operators find out when the application fails during a planned restart or failover.
refuted.argument: Message #3 lists several projects that parse this string, and the patch removes it in exactly the FATAL cases those projects may meet during restarts. The thread does not show that these clients also match the FATAL text or SQLSTATE 57P01. The cost falls on deployed applications that never asked for the change, and the gain is a cleaner message.
refuted.author_must_show: Do the clients listed in message #3 still detect a lost connection after a FATAL such as 57P01 once the appended text is gone?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which rests on the same message #3 evidence and asks for a documented replacement signal.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: libpqwalreceiver and logical replication workers are libpq callers that see CONNECTION_BAD earlier after a FATAL.

touch_points.label: wire protocol
touch_points.reason: libpq reacts differently to an ErrorResponse with FATAL or PANIC severity; no message format changes.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: PQstatus() returns CONNECTION_BAD before the socket closes, and v2 had to change postgres_fdw for it.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry is tagged Bugfix but changes error text and PQstatus() timing that deployed clients depend on; the author targets PG20 only.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: How should applications that match "server closed the connection unexpectedly" detect an admin-terminated connection after the change, and will the docs and release notes say so?
What did postgres_fdw assume about PQstatus() after a FATAL, and have dblink, libpqwalreceiver and the logical replication workers been checked for the same assumption?
How does libpq behave when the FATAL arrives during connection startup, inside COPY, or in pipeline mode?
Does v2 pass the full test suite on Windows, where the client can lose the server's final FATAL message?
Is a change to the message and hint for real unexpected closes left for a separate patch?

committability.owner_note: Andres Freund started the thread and reported the v1 test failures, but nobody has replied to v2. The owner needs to know libpq connection state handling and its in-tree callers.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a behaviour change in every libpq-based client: different error text after a FATAL and earlier CONNECTION_BAD. Reports from drivers, poolers and frameworks can arrive for several releases.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 after the v1 test failures and has moved the entry through three CommitFests.

priority.reason: The goal has agreement and v1 touches one libpq file, but v2 has had no reply across three CommitFests. The v2 patch, including its postgres_fdw change, was not read, so the review cost is an estimate.

provisional_note: The v2 commit message and the postgres_fdw change are not in the material, so the effect on other libpq callers could not be judged. Behaviour during startup, COPY and pipeline mode needs the code.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Move libpq's write_failed mechanism down to pqsecure_raw_write().
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Move libpq's write_failed mechanism down to pqsecure_raw_write().
Reverted commit(s): Restructure libpq's handling of send failures.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Commit 1f39a1c06 implemented write-failure postponement in pqSendSome,
which is above SSL/GSS processing.  However, we've now seen failures
indicating that (some versions of?) OpenSSL have a tendency to report
write failures prematurely too.  Hence, move the primary responsibility
for postponing write failures down to pqsecure_raw_write(), below
SSL/GSS processing.  pqSendSome now sets write_failed only in corner
cases where we'd lost the connection already.

A side-effect of this change is that errors detected in the SSL/GSS
layer itself will be reported immediately (as if they were read
errors) rather than being postponed like write errors.  That's
reverting an effect of 1f39a1c06, and I think it's fine: if there's
not a socket-level error, it's hard to be sure whether an OpenSSL
error ought to be considered a read or write failure anyway.

Another important point is that write-failure postponement is now
effective during connection setup.  OpenSSL's misbehavior of this
sort occurs during SSL_connect(), so that's a change we want.

Per bug #17391 from Nazir Bilal Yavuz.  Possibly this should be
back-patched, but I think it prudent to let it age awhile in HEAD
first.

precedents_retrieved.title: libpq should append error messages, not overwrite
precedents_retrieved.summary: Tom Lane proposed that libpq always append to conn->errorMessage during connection setup and query execution, instead of overwriting it, with only a few defined points that clear it. A second patch labeled each part of the error with the server and port being tried when several hosts are listed.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback because the thread had no activity after August and the patch set no longer applied cleanly. Before that, Robert Haas objected that reporting failures from every host adds noise: when the first host is down and the second rejects a password, the user only needs the password error. Tom Lane did not accept this, and the disagreement was not resolved.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The last status of this patch comes from August, which has been
unanswered.  So I am marking the patch as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 728f86fec65537eade8d9e751961782ddb527934.

The signal handling was a few bricks shy of a load in that commit,
which made the walreceiver non-responsive to SIGTERM while it was

Since it was non-essential refactoring, let's revert it to make v16

keep the branches in sync. The refactoring was a good idea as such,
but it needs a bit more work. Once we have developed a complete patch
with this issue fixed, let's re-apply that to 'master'.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow specifying multiple hosts in libpq connect options
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets libpq accept a comma-separated list of host names, as in `psql -h dbslave,dbmaster`, and try each in turn until one answers. It splits the host string, does a DNS lookup on each name, and links the results into the existing address list.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the patch because the author sent no new version after review. Steve Singer reported that a host name that does not resolve stops the attempt and that error messages print the whole host string. He also said the patch does not cover the master-plus-standby case, all hosts must use one port, and the libpq documentation needs an update. Steve Singer and Bruce Momjian asked for comma-separated full URLs instead of several hosts inside one URL.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Patch marked as returned with feedback, there has been review input,
but unfortunately no patch updates lately.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improve handling of OOM errors in libpq making process hangling for COPY and bind (take 2)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes libpq hangs on out-of-memory errors while it parses COPY start and ParameterDescription messages. The parser leaves pqParseInput3 on error and keeps the first error message, so PQgetResult and PQexecFinish return the failure and do not wait for server input that will not come.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas committed the ParameterDescription fix but did not commit the COPY part. He could not see why the PQexecFinish change was needed, and he found that if getCopyResult() fails with OOM, libpq stays in COPY_IN mode while PQexec() returns NULL, so the next PQexec() fails with "another command is already in progress". Michael Paquier later reported that Heikki could not convince himself the change was sane for the COPY protocol, and planned more testing with tools that use COPY through libpq.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Now, libpq is already in PGASYNC_COPY_IN mode, but PQexec() returned NULL because of the OOM, so the application doesn't know that it's in copy mode.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add last failed connection error message to pg_stat_wal_receiver
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch stores the WAL receiver's last connection failure message in shared memory and shows it as a new last_conn_error column in pg_stat_wal_receiver and pg_stat_get_wal_receiver(). The goal is to let users see why replication connections fail without reading server logs.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier said the patch covers only connection errors and misses other WAL receiver failures, such as an incorrect system ID or a TLI-related report; capturing FATAL errors would need shared memory. He also noted that the string is not reset when the WAL receiver starts, and that pg_stat_wal_receiver returns no rows when pid is NULL, so the column is only visible through the function. The author offered alternatives and said he was fine to withdraw if none was worth pursuing, and the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This stands for the connection error, but there are other things
that could cause a failure down the road, like an incorrect system
ID or a TLI-related report, so that seems a bit limited to me?

precedents_retrieved.title: Improving connection scalability
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Robert Haas, Andres Freund, Tomas Vondra, Jacob Champion
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch applies micro-optimizations to GetSnapshotData(), ComputeXidHorizons() and related code in procarray.c to improve connection scalability. Its main change calls GetSnapshotDataReuse() without first acquiring ProcArrayLock.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas and Andres Freund objected that skipping ProcArrayLock was not shown to be safe, and Tomas Vondra said it was probably broken. With the lock kept, Tomas Vondra's median analysis showed gains of about 0.5-2% that did not grow with client count, so they were possibly noise. Jacob Champion closed it as Returned with Feedback for lack of statistical proof, and the author then said it was best to reject it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Given the conversation so far, I'll go ahead and mark this Returned with
Feedback. Specifically, this patch would need hard statistical proof
that it's having a positive effect.

precedents_retrieved.title: Make all Perl warnings fatal
precedents_retrieved.summary: Replace `use warnings;` with `use warnings FATAL => 'all';` in all Perl scripts in the tree, so that warnings from code generation and TAP tests fail the build or test, similar to -Werror. The patch set also removed an unneeded getprotobyname() call in PostgreSQL/Test/Cluster.pm, which was committed separately.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author returned the patch himself because fatal warnings would first need fixes to the legacy MSVC build system, and he chose to wait for that system's removal. He noted there were no principled objections to the idea.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It looks like there are no principled objections to the overall idea
here, but given this dependency on the MSVC build system removal, I'm
going to set this patch to Returned with feedback for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: postgres_fdw - make cached connection functions tests meaningful with debug_invalidate_system_caches_always
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch sets debug_invalidate_system_caches_always (later renamed debug_discard_caches) to off in the postgres_fdw regression tests, so that cache-clobbering builds stay stable. The tests for postgres_fdw_disconnect, postgres_fdw_disconnect_all and postgres_fdw_get_connections could then show the real function output instead of SELECT 1.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane said the patch assumes that turning debug_discard_caches off means no cache flushes, but flushes can still come at any time from sinval messages sent by other processes such as autovacuum. The tests would then pass most of the time but not always, which is not good enough for the buildfarm. The author agreed and marked the entry rejected.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Not setting
debug_discard_caches doesn't mean that that can't happen, only that
you can't predict when it will happen.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent rejected this idea. P1 shows that on Windows the client can lose the FATAL; that limits the patch's reach and may make tests that expect the new output flaky, but it is no reason to reject the patch. The 2023 discussion Bruce Momjian cites in message #4 is reported only as having reached no conclusion.
Two objections raised; both are fixable with documentation and a clear statement of the PQstatus contract.

The patch changes no on-disk format, WAL or catalog, and adds no new protocol message. It only changes how libpq reacts to an existing ErrorResponse, so the one objection here is about the libpq API seen by callers, including in-tree replication code.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect: libpq drops the appended text and sets CONNECTION_BAD once the server has sent FATAL or PANIC. Who can send a FATAL, for example through pg_terminate_backend(), does not change, and nothing new becomes visible. Without the code I could not check how a FATAL during startup or authentication is handled.
The fix is small, stays inside libpq, and has no hot-path or extension-fit cost. The remaining concerns are about compatibility for existing libpq clients.

No existing libpq option, error verbosity setting or documented idiom stops libpq from appending the "unexpectedly" text after a FATAL or from overwriting the error fields of the final PGresult. This is internal libpq connection-state handling, so an extension or external tool cannot do it, and the patch fixes the existing mechanism instead of adding a second one.

Demand is shown: Andres Freund reports fielding worried user questions about the message (message #1), Haas, Berg and Momjian agree it misleads (messages #2-#4), and the author has hit it repeatedly (message #5). The cost falls on clients that match the appended text after a FATAL, which is a compatibility question for another angle.

warnings: synthesis said NEEDS-COMMITTER-EYES but listed a level 1b objection (standards-compat-1); changed to NEEDS-DESIGN-DISCUSSION
